:::{#def-sensitivity}
#### Sensitivity

Suppose a minimization problem (@def-minimization-problem)
depends on a vector $\vecf{b} \in \reals^m$,
and let $f^*(\vecf{b})$ be its minimum value, as a function of $\vecf{b}$.
When the gradient $\deriv{\vecf{b}} f^*(\vecf{b})$ exists ([gradient](vector-calculus.qmd#def-vector-derivative)),
it is the **sensitivity** of the minimum value to $\vecf{b}$:
by [partial derivative](vector-calculus.qmd#def-partial-derivative), its entry $i$ is the limit,
as a change in $b_i$ alone shrinks to $0$,
of the resulting change in the minimum value divided by the change in $b_i$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-sensitivity}
#### The sensitivity of a one-point problem

Minimize $x^2$ subject to $x = b$, for a number $b$.
The feasible set (@def-feasible-set) is $\cb{b}$, so the minimum value is $f^*(b) = b^2$,
and its sensitivity to $b$ is $\dif{}{b} f^*(b) = 2b$.
At $b = 3$ the sensitivity is $6$:
moving $b$ from $3$ to $3.1$ raises the minimum value from $9$ to $9.61$,
an increase of $0.61$, close to $6 \times 0.1 = 0.6$.

:::
